title: Honest Intervals for Shape Contrasts of Individualized Quantile Treatment Effects at Shrinking Spacing

proof_attempt_summary: D0 corrected the legal smooth bump construction and proved the sparse-side lower and upper claims. D0.5's mathematics review passed, but the original all-sparsity promise remained open: the dense score-stability bound and a matching data-based interval were not proved. Repeating that same directive without a new construction would not close the field-tier gap.
tldr: For the shrinking IQTE shape contrast, the smooth sparse bump family proves the all-interval lower bound \(J_{n,p,s,h}\gtrsim\rho_{n,p,s,h}\) at every studied sparsity level. The projected-score interval in Definition 4 matches it only when \(s\le K_{\mathrm{sp}}\sqrt p\), where \(\rho=\min\{h,\sqrt{hA},hA^{1/3}\}\). For \(\sqrt p\ll s\le p/2\), the only unconditional upper bound is the deterministic \(O(h)\) interval; the sharp dense rate remains open because generic nuisance norms do not control the signed endpoint bias. The target vanishes in every location-shift model, so dense mean-regression bounds do not settle this gap.
gap: Sun and Xia give fixed-quantile IQTE interval theory, while Giessing and Wang give compact-index process convergence. Neither result determines uniformly honest expected length after the quantile spacing shrinks and the leading scores cancel at a smaller scale.
fill: A matched sparse-side theorem combines a legal varying-quantile mixture with projected local scores and exact inactive-sign thresholding. A target-block calibrated dense endpoint is isolated as the only answer-open branch, with a predeclared kill sequence that distinguishes a real proof from a generic nuisance-rate argument.
